mappings.note: Asks what makes a substance biodegradable (micro-organisms can break it down) - the 'distinguishes' clause of C 4.1-LO-1.
Environmental effects of biodegradable substances - the 'consequences of each' clause of LO-1, biodegradable side. Not a disposal-method question, so LO-3 does not apply.
Environmental effects of NON-biodegradable substances - the other half of LO-1's consequences clause.
Defines trophic levels and asks for a food chain with its levels marked - C 2.8-LO-1's 'constructs food chains' clause. No energy arithmetic, so LO-2 is not engaged.

Decomposers break down biodegradable dead matter and return nutrients; the frame has no decomposer outcome, and LO-1 is the only one that owns biodegradation and its environmental consequence. Not LO-2, which is energy arithmetic, and not LO-3, which is human waste disposal.
What ozone is and how it affects life - the ozone outcome C 4.3-LO-2.
Asks the student to propose ways of reducing the waste problem - LO-3's 'proposes ways of reducing the waste a household generates'.
Selects the group of easily biodegradable items - a straight classification, LO-1.
Picks the valid feeding sequence (grass, goat, human) from sets that are not chains - constructing a food chain, C 2.8-LO-1.

Cloth bags, switching off lights, walking - individual practices that reduce waste and consumption, LO-3's 'proposes ways of reducing'. Only partly a waste item (one option is energy saving), but LO-3 is the closest true outcome.
Consequence of wiping out a trophic level - reasoning about the structure of a food chain, C 2.8-LO-1, not the ten per cent arithmetic of LO-2.
Whether the impact differs by trophic level and whether any level is dispensable - trophic-structure reasoning, C 2.8-LO-1.

Biological magnification happens because the chemical is NON-biodegradable and is retained; that is the environmental consequence clause of C 4.1-LO-1. No specific chain is given to order, so LO-1 of C 2.8 is not needed here.
Problems caused by non-biodegradable waste - LO-1's consequences clause. The item asks about effects, not about disposal methods, so LO-3 would be the wrong sibling.
Tests that even wholly biodegradable waste has consequences - the biodegradable side of LO-1's consequences clause.
Why ozone damage matters and what is being done - the 'effects ... and the measures taken to limit it' clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
Fill-in linking a rising standard of living to more waste - LO-3, the outcome about the waste a household generates. Stem carries mojibake (ellipses rendered as 'a¦').
DEFECT: the stem is 'Study the figure. What does it depict?' and no figure is stored, so the topic cannot be established from the text. Cited at the goal CG 4 rather than guessing an outcome.
Producers eat nothing, the top carnivore is not eaten - the ends of a food chain, C 2.8-LO-1.
Why a food chain has only 3-5 steps is C 2.8-LO-2 verbatim ('explain why food chains are limited in length').
Decomposers recycling matter; the mechanism is biodegradation, which only C 4.1-LO-1 covers. C 2.8-LO-1 is about ENERGY flow through trophic levels, and energy is precisely what is NOT recycled.

Answering needs both: why clay and paper are preferable to plastic (biodegradability, LO-1) and why reusable beats disposable at all (waste reduction, C 4.3-LO-3). Neither half alone answers the item.
How hospital waste is disposed of and why - evaluating a method of waste disposal, C 4.3-LO-3.
Skin problems under the Antarctic ozone hole - an EFFECT of ozone depletion, C 4.3-LO-2. The stem never says 'ozone', which is what the item is testing.
The analogy is food chain versus food web - a single supplier and a single buyer is a fragile linear chain. C 2.8-LO-1 is the only outcome covering food webs.

DEFECT: misfiled. A value-based item on the health effects of SMOKING - nothing in this chapter's frame (food chains, ten per cent law, biodegradability, ozone, waste) is true of it. Cited at the goal CG 4 rather than forced onto an outcome.
DEFECT: 'this disaster' has no antecedent - the case passage the item belongs to was not stored, so the topic cannot be established. Cited at the goal CG 4 deliberately.
Why the ozone layer must be protected plus two awareness measures - the effects-and-measures clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
Definition of 'environment'. No outcome in this frame defines it - LO-2 is ozone, LO-3 is waste - so it sits at the competency C 4.3, which covers levels of organisation from organisms to ecosystems.
Cause of ozone depletion in the stratosphere - the 'causes' clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
Naming abiotic components of the environment; the frame has no ecosystem-components outcome, so this rests at competency C 4.3 rather than being forced onto the food-chain outcome.
Biotic and abiotic as the two components of the environment - ecosystem structure, which reaches no LO in this frame, so competency level.
CFCs as the compounds that deplete ozone - the causes clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
Green plants are producers because they fix energy at the first trophic level - the entry point of every food chain, C 2.8-LO-1.
Unidirectional energy flow is C 2.8-LO-1's 'explains the flow of energy through trophic levels'. It asks about direction, not about the ten per cent figure, so LO-2 is the wrong sibling.
Paper beats polythene because paper is biodegradable - LO-1's distinction plus its environmental consequence.
Two steps are both required: order grass-insect-frog-bird into a chain (C 2.8-LO-1), then apply the accumulation of non-biodegradable chemicals up it (C 4.1-LO-1). Neither alone picks the bird.
Paper cups decompose, plastic cups do not - LO-1's biodegradable/non-biodegradable distinction applied to a choice.
Full form of CFC; recall attached to the causes clause of the ozone outcome C 4.3-LO-2.
Explaining 0.5 to 2 to 10 ppm needs the trophic sequence grass-sheep-man (C 2.8-LO-1) and the retention of a non-biodegradable chemical at each step (C 4.1-LO-1).
Objection to CFCs is their destruction of stratospheric ozone - the causes clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
Sorts DDT, crop residue, leather and glass by biodegradability - LO-1's classification clause.
Reduce, reuse, recycle - LO-3's 'proposes ways of reducing the waste a household generates'.

Back-calculating producer energy from 5 J at the top applies the ten per cent law - C 2.8-LO-2. DEFECT: the food chain itself is a figure that was not stored, so the number of steps cannot be read from the text.
Skin cancer from increased UV - an EFFECT of ozone depletion, C 4.3-LO-2.
Naming non-biodegradable wastes - LO-1's classification clause.
Definition of biomagnification, which rests on the substance being non-biodegradable - LO-1. No chain is supplied to order, so a second code is not needed.
DEFECT: 'What is depicted in the scheme?' with no scheme stored - the topic cannot be established from the text. Cited at the goal CG 4 rather than guessed.
Ozone is toxic at ground level yet shields us in the stratosphere - the function half of C 4.3-LO-2.
Picking the producers (rose, neem) from a mixed list is assigning first trophic level - C 2.8-LO-1.
Without decomposers, biodegradable matter would not be broken down and nutrients would not return - the environmental consequence clause of C 4.1-LO-1, the only outcome that covers biodegradation.
The five organisms must first be ordered into grass-grasshopper-frog-snake-peacock (C 2.8-LO-1) before biomagnification (C 4.1-LO-1) identifies the peacock.

Two different outcomes in one item: maximum available energy is the ten per cent law pointing at the phytoplankton (C 2.8-LO-2), maximum pesticide is biomagnification pointing at the bird (C 4.1-LO-1). Answering one does not answer the other. Stem has mojibake arrows ('aa>').
Man-made ecosystems (crop field, aquarium) - ecosystem types, which no LO in this frame covers, so competency C 4.3. Stored concept tag 'Energy Flow in Ecosystems' is wrong; no energy is discussed.
Sorts glass, leather, glucose and silver foil by biodegradability - LO-1.
Methods of garbage disposal - LO-3's 'evaluates methods of waste disposal'.
Why ozone depletion is a concern - the effects clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
Ways of reducing the waste-disposal problem - LO-3. DEFECT: duplicate of qid:87205, same question with 'ways' for 'methods'.
Plant-Man beats Plant-Goat-Man because each extra step loses ninety per cent - the ten per cent law, C 2.8-LO-2, not merely the shape of the chain.
Refrigerants and fire-extinguisher halons as ozone-depleting compounds - the causes clause of C 4.3-LO-2.
